check_cluster.description: Check that a datacenter's Consul servers have a leader (without one, Consul can't answer or change anything), with its servers.
check_cluster.name: check_cluster

parameters.description: The datacenter, such as dc1. Leave blank for the connection's.
parameters.name: datacenter

datacenters.description: Every datacenter Consul knows, the nearest first

healthy.description: True when the datacenter has a leader

leader.description: The leading server's address, such as 10.0.0.5:8300; empty for none

delete_key.description: Delete a key, or every key under a prefix. Consul keeps no history, so a deleted key can't be brought back.
delete_key.name: delete_key

parameters.description: The key to delete, or the prefix with 'Everything under it', such as config/old-app/.
parameters.name: key

parameters.description: Delete every key that starts with this, for good.
parameters.name: recurse

parameters.description: A modify index from 'Get key value': the key is deleted only if nothing changed it since. Leave blank to delete it anyway.
parameters.name: cas_index

parameters.description: The datacenter, such as dc1. Leave blank for the connection's.
parameters.name: datacenter

deleted.description: False when there was nothing there to delete

recurse.description: True when everything under it was deleted

fire_event.description: Send a Consul user event, such as deploy, to every node or only those running a service. Scripts set up with consul watch on the nodes act on it.
fire_event.name: fire_event

parameters.description: The event's name, as the watches expect it, such as deploy.
parameters.name: event_name

parameters.description: A short text to send with it, such as a version, up to about 300 characters.
parameters.name: payload

parameters.description: Only nodes running this service. Leave blank for every node.
parameters.name: service_filter

parameters.description: Only nodes running the service with this tag, such as canary.
parameters.name: tag_filter

parameters.description: Only nodes whose names match this pattern, such as web-.*.
parameters.name: node_filter

parameters.description: The datacenter, such as dc1. Leave blank for the connection's.
parameters.name: datacenter

node_filter.description: Only nodes matching this got it

service_filter.description: Only nodes running this service got it

tag_filter.description: Only nodes running the service with this tag got it

get_key.description: Read a key's value, such as a feature flag or a setting, to use in a later step. A key that isn't set comes back with found false and an empty value rather than failing the step.
get_key.name: get_key

parameters.description: The key, as Consul's Key/Value page shows it, such as config/app/feature_x.
parameters.name: key

parameters.description: The datacenter, such as dc1. Leave blank for the connection's.
parameters.name: datacenter

create_index.description: Consul's index when the key was created

flags.description: The number stored with the key by whoever wrote it; usually 0

found.description: False when the key isn't set; its value is then empty

is_text.description: False when the value isn't text, such as a file, and is given as base64

json.description: The value read as JSON, when it is a JSON object or list; empty otherwise

link.description: A link to the key in Consul

locked.description: True while a Consul lock session holds the key

modify_index.description: Consul's index when the key last changed; give it to 'Set key value' to write only if nothing changed it since

value.description: The value as text (base64 when it isn't text)

get_keys.description: Read every key under a prefix, such as an app's settings in config/app/, as one object, up to 1000 keys.
get_keys.name: get_keys

parameters.description: The folder to read, such as config/app/. Keys under it come back without it.
parameters.name: prefix

parameters.description: The datacenter, such as dc1. Leave blank for the connection's.
parameters.name: datacenter

data.description: Each key without the prefix, with its value, such as db/host

items.description: Each key with its value and indexes, in order

create_index.description: Consul's index when it was created

flags.description: The number stored with the key; usually 0

is_text.description: False when the value is given as base64

modify_index.description: Consul's index when it last changed

relative_key.description: The key without the prefix, such as db/host

value.description: Its value as text (base64 when it isn't text)

prefix.description: The prefix read, such as config/app/

tree.description: The same values nested by folder, such as db then host; a key that is also a folder keeps its value under _value

truncated.description: True when there were more keys than Lodol reads at once

get_service_health.description: See how a service is doing for a status report: how many instances are passing, warning and critical, and what each failing check printed.
get_service_health.display_str_template: Get the health of Consul service {0}.
get_service_health.name: get_service_health

parameters.description: The service's name, such as web.
parameters.name: service

parameters.description: The datacenter, such as dc1. Leave blank for the connection's.
parameters.name: datacenter

failing_checks.description: Each check that isn't passing, with what it printed

healthy.description: True when every instance passes every check

link.description: A link to the service in Consul

status.description: The worst instance's status: passing, warning or critical

warning.description: Instances whose worst check is warning

list_health_checks.description: List the health checks that are failing (or critical, warning, passing, or every one) across the datacenter, or for one service or node, with what each printed.
list_health_checks.name: list_health_checks

parameters.description: Which checks to list.
parameters.name: state

parameters.description: Only this service's checks. Leave blank for every service.
parameters.name: service

parameters.description: Only checks on this node. Leave blank for every node.
parameters.name: node

parameters.description: The datacenter, such as dc1. Leave blank for the connection's.
parameters.name: datacenter

checks.description: The checks, critical first, then by node

check_type.description: http, tcp, ttl, script and so on; empty for Consul's own

link.description: A link to the instance's or node's checks in Consul

maintenance.description: True for the check that maintenance mode adds

node.description: The node the check runs on

notes.description: Notes whoever set the check up gave it

service_id.description: The service instance it checks; empty for the node itself

service_name.description: The service it checks; empty for the node itself

state.description: The checks asked for: failing, critical, warning, passing or any

list_nodes.description: List the nodes (machines) in a datacenter with their addresses and whether Consul can reach them.
list_nodes.name: list_nodes

parameters.description: The datacenter, such as dc1. Leave blank for the connection's.
parameters.name: datacenter

failing_checks.description: The names of its own checks that aren't passing

link.description: A link to the node in Consul

maintenance.description: True while the node is in maintenance mode

status.description: The worst of its own checks: passing, warning or critical

list_service_instances.description: List a service's instances with the address and port to reach each, its tags and its health, or only the healthy ones.
list_service_instances.display_str_template: List the instances of Consul service {0}.
list_service_instances.name: list_service_instances

parameters.description: The service's name, such as web.
parameters.name: service

parameters.description: Leave out instances with a warning or critical check.
parameters.name: passing_only

parameters.description: Only instances with this tag, such as canary.
parameters.name: tag

parameters.description: The datacenter, such as dc1. Leave blank for the connection's.
parameters.name: datacenter

address.description: The address to reach it at

checks.description: Its health checks, its node's included

id.description: The instance's ID, such as web-1

link.description: A link to the instance in Consul

maintenance.description: True while it, or its node, is in maintenance mode

status.description: The worst of its checks: passing, warning or critical

passing_only.description: True when only instances passing every check are listed

tag.description: The tag asked for, if one was

list_services.description: List the services registered in Consul, with their tags, or only those with a tag.
list_services.name: list_services

parameters.description: The datacenter, such as dc1. Leave blank for the connection's.
parameters.name: datacenter

parameters.description: Only services with this tag, such as api.
parameters.name: tag

link.description: A link to the service in Consul

name.description: The service's name, such as web

tag.description: The tag asked for, if one was

set_key.description: Set a key's value, such as turning a feature flag on, creating the key if it isn't there. With 'Only if unchanged since', a change someone else made in between is caught rather than overwritten.
set_key.name: set_key

parameters.description: The key, as Consul's Key/Value page shows it, such as config/app/feature_x.
parameters.name: key

parameters.description: The value to store, such as true. Leave blank for an empty value.
parameters.name: value

parameters.description: A modify index from 'Get key value': the change is refused if anything changed the key since. 0 writes only if the key doesn't exist yet. Leave blank to write whatever is there.
parameters.name: cas_index

parameters.description: The datacenter, such as dc1. Leave blank for the connection's.
parameters.name: datacenter

create_index.description: Consul's index when it was created

created.description: True when the key didn't exist before

link.description: A link to the key in Consul

set_maintenance.description: Put a service's instances into maintenance mode, such as before a deploy, so Consul stops sending traffic to them, or take them out again. Works for instances registered with the Consul agent at the connection's address.
set_maintenance.display_str_template: Set maintenance mode for Consul service {0}.
set_maintenance.name: set_maintenance

parameters.description: The service's name, such as web.
parameters.name: service

parameters.description: One instance, such as web-1. Leave blank for every instance of the service registered with this agent.
parameters.name: instance

parameters.description: On to put them into maintenance, off to take them out.
parameters.name: enable

parameters.description: Why, shown in Consul, such as Deploying 2.5.0.
parameters.name: reason

instances.description: The instances put into (or out of) maintenance

link.description: A link to the service in Consul

maintenance.description: True when they were put into maintenance, false when taken out

reason.description: The reason given, shown in Consul

description: Read and change Consul's key/value settings, see services, their instances and health for status reports, put instances into maintenance around a deploy, and fire events. Start a workflow when a health check goes critical or recovers, or when a key changes.

hashicorp_consul_check_critical_trigger.description: Runs when a health check goes critical, for every service or one, with what the check printed, such as to alert someone. Maintenance mode doesn't start it, and checks already critical when the workflow is turned on don't either.

parameters.description: Only this service's checks, such as web. Leave blank for every check, the nodes' own included.
parameters.name: service

hashicorp_consul_check_recovered_trigger.description: Runs when a health check that was critical or warning is passing again, for every service or one, such as to close an alert.

parameters.description: Only this service's checks, such as web. Leave blank for every check, the nodes' own included.
parameters.name: service

hashicorp_consul_key_changed_trigger.description: Runs when a key under a prefix is created, changed or deleted, with its new value, such as to act on a feature flag or a setting. Keys already there when the workflow is turned on don't start it.

parameters.description: Only keys under this folder, such as config/app/. Leave blank for every key (up to 1000).
parameters.name: prefix
